title: Tunable flat bands from a parent chiral Hamiltonian
authors: Jun-Hyung Bae, Alexei Andreanov, Saurabh Maiti
abstract: Systems with flat bands are interesting as they potentially host many exotic quantum phenomena that would be hard to observe in usual systems with dispersive bands. Multiple approaches were developed to construct flat band systems, with most of them requiring fine-tuning and/or solving a challenging inverse-eigenvalue problem. In this article we work with an idea that uses a parent bipartite system to generate a family of flat bands by means of Hilbert space projections. This method is largely free from fine-tuning constraints and allows us to identify conditions for a Hamiltonian to guarantee flat bands at desired energies, with desired degree of degeneracy. We also show that one can control the touching points of the flat band with dispersive bands at any desirable point in the Brillouin zone. In the process, we identify perturbations that preserve the flat bands or split them controllably. This approach provides easy tunability in designing flat band systems with desired properties.
summary: This paper presents a powerful theoretical framework to design flat band systems by utilizing Hilbert space projections from a parent bipartite Hamiltonian. This method is highly advantageous because it avoids the need for fine-tuning parameters or solving difficult inverse problems. The key result is a general, computable bound for the number of flat bands, providing unprecedented tunability in designing quantum materials with desired electronic properties.
main_problem: Developing general, fine-tuning-free methods to construct and characterize tunable flat band systems in condensed matter models.
main_result: The authors show that flat bands can be robustly generated by performing Hilbert space projections from a parent bipartite system, and they derive a general bound to estimate the number of flat bands without solving the full spectrum.
method: The core method involves using Löwdin projection techniques on a bipartite Hamiltonian, which allows the preservation of flat band structure even when the projection energy is varied or when the resulting Hamiltonian loses its bipartite nature.
model_or_system: The study focuses on bipartite Hamiltonians, $H$, partitioned into smaller ($S$) and larger ($L$) subsystems. The analysis is applied to lattice models, such as the superhoneycomb lattice, to demonstrate the principle.
key_observables: The number of zero eigenvalues (nullity) at a specific energy, which quantifies the number of flat bands ($\phi$).
important_parameters: The relative sizes of the subsystems ($n$ and $m$), and the energy scale of the projection ($E_0$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the system being bipartite for the initial construction, and the general bound derivation assumes certain block-independence properties for equality to hold.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates band distortion upon projection, while Figure 2 demonstrates that the projection procedure preserves flat bands (marked in red) even when projecting at energies away from the flat band energy.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of flat band construction, details the projection method using bipartite Hamiltonian partitioning, derives general bounds for flat band counting using nullity arguments, and concludes by showing how perturbations can control the touching points and splitting of these bands.
why_interesting: The robust, structural approach to generating flat bands bypasses the need for solving complex inverse eigenvalue problems, offering a powerful, general design tool for realizing exotic quantum phenomena in engineered materials.
